Subject: Internal: preliminary Redwood repro notes for Nimba MAP

Team —

I kicked off an initial repro on our sandbox cluster (same model hash as MAP, quantized 8-bit, batcher=continuous) and compared to Rahul’s CSV. Early findings:

- Warmup variance: Rahul’s runs appear to have shorter warmup (5 inferences) vs our 30s steady-state. That can inflate TTFT medians.
- KV-cache priming: their PerfKit default keeps KV-cache cold between certain scenarios; when we forced the cache to remain hot TTFT dropped ~30ms.
- Tokenization mismatch: there’s a small discrepancy in byte-pair tokenizer versions used by their docker image (v2.0 vs our v2.1) causing ~2% token count diff for a subset of prompts.
- GPU kernel selection: their infra uses cuda 12.4 + cuDNN X, our sandbox was on cuda 12.1 — not a huge effect but worth noting for tail latency.

Attached: perf_run_agg_20260727.csv (redwood side). Action items:
- Karthik: produce exact command snippet and container tag to share with customer (owner)
- Dylan: confirm joint run cadence and invite list (owner)
- Vanessa: update MAP spreadsheet with repro milestones and close date (owner)

I’ll follow up with a micro-run comparison table once Karthik’s commands are executed.

— Marissa
Marissa Cole

Rahul —

Sharing the exact reproducibility commands we used on our side. If you run these on your cluster (same container tag) we should get comparable telemetry. Please run both and paste the resulting CSVs back into this thread.

Commands (assumes PerfKit v1.3.0 and nvidia runtime):

1) Baseline (KV-cache ON, 30s warmup):
perfkit run --image=redwood/infer:2026-07-10 --batcher=continuous --kv-cache=on --warmup=30 --concurrency=1..80 --tokens=128,512 --out=redwood_baseline.csv

2) Isolate warmup/KV (KV-cache OFF, 5-run warmup):
perfkit run --image=redwood/infer:2026-07-10 --batcher=continuous --kv-cache=off --warmup=5 --concurrency=1..80 --tokens=128,512 --out=redwood_no_kvcache.csv

Notes:
- Container tag: redwood/infer:2026-07-10 (includes tokenizer v2.1 and quantization flags --q8-mode=plus)
- Kernel/CUDA: tested on cuda 12.1 + driver 545; small tail differences expected on 12.4
- Sampling: set --samples=200 for median stability

Quick preliminary numbers from our baseline run (summary):
- TTFT median @128 tokens: 160ms
- TTFT median @512 tokens: 480ms
- Max sustained concurrency (no errors): 62

If your numbers still differ after matching image and flags, please also share your docker/container runtime (nvidia-docker vs containerd), and kernel driver versions.

— Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Principal Perf Engineer, Redwood Inference

Team —

Quick update from our side after running Karthik’s two commands (attached nimba_run_results_20260730.csv and repro_steps.md):

- When we matched the container tag (redwood/infer:2026-07-10) and used --samples=200 plus warmup=30, our TTFT median @128 tokens dropped to ~170ms — within ~6% of Redwood’s baseline.
- With KV-cache enabled and hot (cache primed), our max sustainable concurrency increased to ~59.
- The remaining delta appears to be due to our cluster’s kernel/CUDA mismatch (we’re on cuda 12.4) and also how PerfKit cycles idle workers — we’ll try the container runtime change (containerd -> nvidia-docker) next.

Conclusion: we’re comfortable accepting the MAP numbers with a short appendix documenting the methodology differences (warmup and KV-cache behavior). Please update the MAP spreadsheet with that appendix and we’ll move to procurement next week.

Thanks for the quick turnaround. Next steps:
- Vanessa: finalize MAP and trigger sign-off doc
- Dylan: you’ll follow up on quote/discount and procurement contacts
- Marissa/Karthik: prepare the perf appendix for inclusion in the contract

— Rahul
